Right. The way to think of it is this:

Explosion: body of matter in which fire is happening

So when there's an explosion, there is always expanding gases? So like, the explosion is just the trigger, whilst the expanding gases is the effect of the trigger.

Right. Remember the pervert formula: pv=nrt. When the explosion happens, the matter there goes from probably about the ambient temperature to the temperature it has burned at. Well, gases expand when they're warmed. But immediately following combustion, the gases in question have gotten hot very very fast. So, they're in a rush to satisfy pv=nrt, which says they should have a much larger volume than they do. Hence--expanding gases.

Does this mean that expanding gases (caused by an explosion) that travel at a faster speeds always have to be triggered by a higher-temperature explosion? In other words: Speed of gas = Temperature of explosion?

I'm gonna go with "more or less" before I speak out of my expertise, but I can say with certainty that it's a combination of "temperature of explosion" and the average density of exhaust products. Gunpowder has a lot of carbon, but after the explosion, much of it is bound up with oxygen as CO2. Since CO2 is a gas, with an average density, and it's also heated, it's compelled to expand rapidly.

Chemically, you have low explosives and high explosives. Low explosives are things like gun powder, flash powder, and black powder. They deflagrate (combust) at a speed below the seed of sound and create gas.

High explosives are things like TNT and C4. They chemically decompose faster than the speed of sound (detonate) and produce a lot of gas.

Mechanically, if you over-pressuruze a container until it reaches structural failure, it is commonly said to explode, even though there is no chemical reaction.
So TLDR: "Explosion = A bunch of expanding gas".

Momentum and energy density.

Every particle has some momentum, potential energy, and kinetic energy. The particles of expanding gas have lower momentum and kinetic energy than particles in an explosion.

This is confusing, since other people are saying that explosion = a bunch of expanding gas. But let's say you are the one in the right, do you know where one draws the line between an explosion and "just" expanding gases?

It's an explosion when each particle's forward momentum can be transfered to nearby particles in such a way that a shockwave is formed and an increase in pressure is measured. Shockwave is a consequence of material density, speed, and how the material is contained.
Does that mean you can technically trigger an explosion "within" a piece of steel or wood or something?

Sure. Every time you hear crackling or popping of wood on a fire it is an internal explosion. However, metalic crystalline structures like steel have homogeneous molecular structures and very strong chemical bonds. This results in fairly uniform and slow thermal expansion and a tendency to not fly apart randomly. On the other hand when radioactive elements are assembled properly they do explode, see Hiroshima and Nagisaki.

**Daily Devotional**

**June 13**

*17 Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. (Matthew 5:17 KJV)*

Jesus didn’t come to destroy the Law, but to fulfill it, and He did. Jesus needed to tell people His purpose for coming, and since He was preaching mercy and grace, He needed to let people know that He was fulfilling the Law. By His fulfilling the whole law, and living a completely sinless life (1 Peter 2:22), He was able to become the perfect sacrifice that did fulfill the requirements of the law for all our sins (1 John 2:2). Jesus didn’t do away with the law, but just lived it. Once the Law was fulfilled, and the perfect sacrifice was made, then the Law no longer had control of our lives. Since the Law was what made sin come alive (Romans 7:9), the fulfilling of the Law did away with sin. Christians should not be sin conscious at all now (Hebrews 10:2).

The Law is still in effect for all those who do not accept Jesus as their Savior, as they are turning down His sacrifice for their sins. Sins have been totally done away with as far as God is concerned, and that means for the whole world (1 John 2:2). The only sin that will send a non-believer to hell is the sin of rejecting Jesus, and anyone who does so, deserves what they will get. To scorn the tremendous sacrifice of Jesus is by far the worse sin anyone could ever commit. Make Jesus your Savior (Romans 10:9-10), and don’t blasphemy the Holy Ghost (Matthew 12:31-32) or become reprobate (Romans 1:28), or disobey Jesus (Hebrews 5:9), and you will make it to heaven – Praise God.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
